summary: Tested the OpenAI TTS loudness fix end to end with ElevenLabs out of quota (401 quota_exceeded, so every line falls back to OpenAI tts-1/sage). New audio is loud: /api/speak -16.4 LUFS / -0.4 dBTP over 8.0s; /api/agent?speak=true 'I need fuel' part 1 -16.3 LUFS / -1.7 dBTP, part 2 -17.5 LUFS / +0.1 dBTP. Raw OpenAI was about -26 to -33 LUFS. Audio is audio/mpeg and decodes, Range bytes=0-1023 returns 206 with the correct Content-Range and bytes, and duration matches the raw clip within 0.1s. louder() takes about 16-20 ms, and /api/speak took 1.2-3.6s, the same as or faster than a direct tts-1 call (1.9-2.7s). louder(b'garbage') and louder(b'') return the input unchanged. Web smoke test at 390x844 passed: access code TRUCK2026, skip onboarding, Type 'I need fuel', reply and route to Roady's Truck Stop shown, voice/audio requests 206, no console errors. One minor problem: 42 old, unboosted OpenAI clips (24kHz/128k, -26 to -33 LUFS) are still saved on disk in backend/.tts_cache.

minor.issue: 42 of 334 saved clips are unboosted OpenAI tts-1 audio from before the fix (24000 Hz, 128 kb/s, -26 to -33 LUFS). They are stored under the key 'openai|tts-1|sage|<text>', so they are not used while ELEVENLABS is set up, which is the current setup. If the ElevenLabs key is removed, or a request sets voice/model explicitly, /api/speak serves these quiet clips without boosting them, which brings back the user's 'very quiet' bug for fixed lines (onboarding, fillers).

54 saved ElevenLabs clips (44.1kHz/96k) are only -21 to -25 LUFS. The boosted OpenAI fallback is now about -16 LUFS, so these lines play 5-8 dB quieter than the fallback lines mixed with them. This is a volume mismatch, not a regression.

action_items: Stale quiet saved clips: add a boost version to the OpenAI branch of voice.cache_tag (e.g. 'openai|tts-1|sage|g13'), or delete the 24kHz/128k files in backend/.tts_cache, so old unboosted audio can never be served.
Optional: make loudness consistent by also normalizing saved ElevenLabs lines that are below about -20 LUFS, or check the ElevenLabs voice output level.
critical_code_review_comments: louder() is safe: 5s timeout, returns the input on a non-zero exit code or empty output, and the subprocess is async, so the event loop is not blocked.
If wait_for times out, the ffmpeg process is not killed (no p.kill()), so it can be left orphaned. Add p.kill() in the timeout path.
The alimiter limit is 0.84 on sample peak, but true peak can reach +0.1 dBTP (seen on agent part 2). This is acceptable for phones but is not strictly at or below 0 dBTP.
conftest.py quietly adds a Bearer token to every requests.Session request. Auth-negative tests must pass their own Authorization header, otherwise they give false 200s.
seed_data_creation: None. The /api/speak tests create 'TEST loudness check xxxx' and 'Probe xxxx' fallback clips in the in-memory cache only; fallback audio is not saved to disk.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Measure loudness with imageio_ffmpeg loudnorm print_format=summary. Duration from pipe input shows as N/A, so read the last time= value instead. ElevenLabs quota is exhausted, so every TTS call goes through the OpenAI fallback and louder(). Run tests with -n0 to see print output (pytest.ini uses xdist).
rca_of_issue: Original bug: OpenAI tts-1 mp3 is about 12 dB quieter than ElevenLabs. Confirmed fixed for new audio (about -16 LUFS). What remains is old unboosted OpenAI clips saved to disk before the fix (see minor issue).
